conventions.convention: Inner products are linear in the first argument; projection coefficients are ⟨x,e⟩, while ⟨e,ψ_z⟩ contains conjugated coherent-state coefficients.
The transverse space consists of almost-everywhere classes in L²(R³;C³) satisfying k·f(k)=0. Π(0)=0; changing the value at this null point changes no L² operator.
Radiation assignments are adopted in a declared inertial chart: k has units m⁻¹, ω=c|k|, E=ℏω and p=ℏk. No Lorentz transformation law or Galilean covariance of radiation is asserted.

Wavepacket normalization uses d³k, so normalized coordinate representatives have units m^(3/2). Coherent labels z are dimensionless. A normalisable mode is a ray in the transverse space; a sharp propagation label is a spectral parameter.

Fock indices include zero, with vacuum sector C and zero vacuum energy and momentum. Total signed momentum uses the maximal domain of the summed multiplier, without separate integrability requirements on its summands.
The analyser labels +1 and −1 mean transmitted and blocked; the spectral values of Pθ are 1 and 0. Conditional Lüders updates require positive outcome probability.
Finite energy second moments require φ∈D(ε); literal pairings involving ε² or T_n² additionally require the stated square-operator domains.
Ideal count and energy-window laws supply single-measurement probabilities. Repetition requires a separate sampling model; destructive detectors require separately declared instruments.

The geometric preparation uses independently declared ε₀>0 joules and β>0 J⁻¹. It asserts neither thermal equilibrium nor a temperature identification. Gibbs compression has the generally β-dependent scale −β⁻¹log⟨e^(−βε)φ,φ⟩.

load_bearing.statement: Adopts a two-dimensional transverse polarisation model, the bosonic transverse radiation Fock sector, and the assignments ω=c|k|, E=ℏω and p=ℏk in a declared inertial chart, with the stated observable domains and physical limitations.

Under Countable Choice and Choice, for a unit φ∈H, Uφ:F(C)→F(H) is an isometry onto the closed fixed-mode subspace, intertwines sector, number and ladder operators on the stated domains, and gives the displayed energy first and second moments under the specified ε and ε² domain hypotheses.

Under Countable Choice and Choice, the transverse restrictions of multiplication by ℏk_j and ℏc|k| are self-adjoint on their maximal square-integrability domains, have inverse-image spectral projections and push-forward laws, have no eigenvalues, and have strictly positive variance for every unit vector in their respective domains.

Under Countable Choice and Choice, the signed summed momentum multipliers are self-adjoint on their maximal symmetric transverse sector domains; their self-adjoint Fock direct sums have the stated sectorwise spectral measures, scalar push-forward sum and vacuum atom at zero.

For a two-dimensional complex inner-product space with the stated orthonormal basis and linear-first convention, the displayed rotated vectors yield complementary orthogonal projections, overlap cos(θ−φ), squared projection cos²(θ−φ), and the stated periodicity and ray invariance.

Declares ideal total-number detection by Fock sector projections, ideal energy-window detection by the free-energy spectral projections, and polarisation-analyser detection, with Lüders readings where specified and separate sampling and destructive-detector requirements.

concerns.concern: Statement (d) ends 'so neither preparation has sharp energy', although the statement permits n=0 and z=0. Both then give the vacuum Ω, and H_fΩ=0, so their energy law is δ₀. The displayed variances correctly vanish in these cases. The non-sharp conclusion needs explicit restriction to n≥1 and z≠0; otherwise this public conclusion is false. The preceding positivity sentence may suggest those restrictions, but the concluding wording does not state them.

Proof 3.1 defines m_n:=m·1_{|m|≤n}, a function on R³, and then writes 'm_n(E_h)' and an integral of m_n against E_h. E_h is a PVM on R, so these expressions have the wrong function domain. The immediate reconstruction is to define b_n(t)=t·1_{|t|≤n} on R and use b_n(E_h), with m_n=b_n∘m. The resulting multiplier argument is sound.

alerts.finding: The Statement says 'the bounded resolvent is the multiplier (λ−z)⁻¹'. The library definition def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator fixes R_A(z)=(zI−A)⁻¹, whose multiplier is (z−λ)⁻¹. Proof 6.1 correctly constructs (A−z)⁻¹, but this is the negative of the defined resolvent. For A=0 on C and z=1 the stated multiplier gives −I, whereas the defined resolvent is I. The norm estimate and the PVM-uniqueness clauses used by batch 63 are unaffected.

seams_checked.note: Uses symmetric sectors and adopted bosonic statistics. Radiation data are declared separately; the massive species model is not used to derive photon spin or a massless limit.

Fock, ladder and number domains match the suppliers. The transverse free-energy supplier's DC/AC hypotheses are carried. Its proof 5.1 supplies the cited direct-sum PVM, and its noncompactness conclusion is used only for the full continuum Gibbs operator.

Tensor, finite-component Euclidean product, permutation and scalar multiplier statements retain their hypotheses. Transverse and symmetric restrictions are established locally rather than attributed to a stronger supplier statement.
Total-momentum construction cites uniqueness of regular representing PVMs faithfully. It does not use the supplier's resolvent-sign sentence identified in the alert.

Retains state, Born, update, apparatus and SI conventions while explicitly adopting a separate radiation extension. The momentum-source qualification agrees with [Littlejohn, Section 7](https://bohr.physics.berkeley.edu/classes/221/notes/quantemf.pdf): normal ordering, Coulomb gauge and box normalization.
Pure preparations use normalized rank-one ray states; general preparations use positive trace-class operators of trace one. Radiation use is explicitly authorized by the extension postulate.
Uses spectral Born measures, atom/eigenspace correspondence and mixture affinity. First moments are distinguished from operator domains; finite variances retain square-integrability hypotheses.
Finite/countable projective outcome structures and Lüders updates retain positive-probability conditions. Destructive detection is explicitly outside the declared instrument class.
Preserves declared units and apparatus/sampling qualifications. No example reports measurements or infers empirical certainty.
Nonzero amplitude data are normalized before their quantum reading; geometric mixtures have nonnegative weights summing to one.

Count and bin probabilities use the declared Born laws. Equality with classical intensity fractions is a conditional comparison; the polarisation source agrees with this limited comparison in [Binney and Skinner, Section 1.3.6](https://www-thphys.physics.ox.ac.uk/people/JamesBinney/qb.pdf).
Gibbs-compression calculation uses regular spectral uniqueness faithfully, without using the alerted resolvent convention.

Single-mode thermal weights are transferred with the supplier's positive parameter set to the independently declared effective energy. Compression is distinguished from invariant restriction and from a full-sector Gibbs density.
Trace-norm mixture and finite-product integral uses retain the supplier hypotheses and Euclidean scope.
The arbitrary complex bin pair is declared directly as an ideal sharp measurement; it is not falsely identified with the original real-angle analyser family.

The coupled-model definition uses the declared transverse Fock space, vacuum, sectors and H_f. Spectral detection uses the one-photon push-forward law only after normalization; η₀=0 is explicitly excluded from that preparation construction.
The spectral-density thought experiment uses ideal energy-window probabilities faithfully and distinguishes finite-time normalisable photon laws from a separately declared sharp-line idealisation.
